# Mental Squeeze Point (LYT)

A mental squeeze point is, in Nick Milo's glossary, the moment in any endeavour when the amount of information starts to overwhelm you. You either get past it or the work stalls.

According to Milo, this is the cue to build a Map of Content: become a cartographer of your own content and gather the scattered notes in one place. He ties it to note volume. With around 100 to 500 notes, favourite notes get hard to find and you start gravitating toward maps; with thousands, you want structures for your structures. The same signal works top-down, to make sense of existing knowledge.

He advises avoiding premature structure. Waiting for the squeeze keeps Fluid Frameworks (LYT) earned by use.
